name: VOR Depth Selection
summary: Look at the target and shake your head: the ratio of eye to head rotation during the shake reveals how far away you are looking, which tells apart objects that overlap along the gaze line.
howItWorks: While the user keeps gaze on a target and deliberately shakes the head, the vestibulo-ocular reflex counter-rotates the eyes; the eye-to-head angular velocity ratio (VOR gain) is larger for nearer fixation points, so it gives the gaze depth after a per-user depth calibration. It works with one eye and without accurate gaze calibration (pupil movement in the eye image suffices). The head-shake doubles as the selection trigger, and the candidate whose depth matches the estimate is selected. In a VR study (N=11, HTC Vive with Tobii eye tracking) with pairs of partly overlapping targets at 0.3–7 m, selections took 0.56 s on average; accuracy matched vergence-based depth up to 1 m and was 18% better at larger distances. Natural head shifts without a deliberate shake did not work.

relationships.note: Adds gaze-depth estimation from head-shake VOR to resolve depth ambiguity.
